AI Summary

The can't-miss paper this period is **TIPs** (Genome Biology, 10.1186/s13059-026-04191-y): a deep-learning-guided immunopeptidomics framework that expands the landscape of **HLA-presented, TE-derived antigens** by taming the inflated search space. This lands directly on the lab's HLA/TE-regulation program (Atma) and the broader thesis that TEs supply immunologically visible, cancer-relevant sequence — worth reading against the LCL CUT&RUN / MHC-graph analysis and the IFNAR2 cancer-immunotherapy angle. Two more are essential: Cedric Feschotte's **Nature Reviews Genetics** review, 'Transposable elements as catalysts of evolutionary innovation' (10.1038/s41576-026-00980-0), the cleanest current framing of the lab's central argument; and Schnabl-Baumgartner et al. in **Molecular Cell** (10.1016/j.molcel.2026.06.024), showing the ChAHP complex silences **SINE B2** elements not by heterochromatin but by physically blocking TFIIIB/Pol III recruitment — a distinct 'off switch' for the very B2 SINEs the lab activates as IFN-inducible enhancers (Horton/Kelly, eLife 2023).

On regulatory evolution, two MBE papers reinforce the lab's terrain: ~50% of human CTCF sites are conserved and purifying-selected at TAD boundaries while human-specific sites show positive selection and **partly derive from TEs** (10.1093/molbev/msag167), and segmental duplications build >1,000 human co-regulatory element families with human-specific rewiring enriched in immune/neural networks (10.1093/molbev/msag140) — a mechanism parallel to TE-mediated network formation. For the computational side, SAGE-net (Nature Methods, 10.1038/s41592-026-03124-8) benchmarks **sequence-to-function** models on personal genomes, directly relevant to the AlphaGenome effort's inter-individual prediction problem.

cGAS-STING remains busy and cancer-facing: tumor lactate directly binds and inhibits STING (Immunity, 10.1016/j.immuni.2026.06.004; reversible with PKM2 inhibition + anti-PD-1), and an mRNA-LNP vaccine co-delivers STING agonists for antitumor T-cell priming (PNAS, 10.1073/pnas.2525718123). Two RNA-splicing items connect to the IFNAR2 decoy-exon / ASO strategy: circular ADAR-recruiting RNAs achieve long-term exon-skipping rescue of DMD in NHPs and patients (Cell, 10.1016/j.cell.2026.05.030), and plant NLR immunity is gated by mRNA alternative splicing (Science, 10.1126/science.adx9929). FOSL1 driving a super-enhancer program in scarring (Cell Reports, 10.1016/j.celrep.2026.117647-adjacent 117667) is a useful AP-1/super-enhancer parallel to LTR10 biology.
